hook: Software quality is nose-diving, and LLMs are accelerating it.

beats.say: Because of large language models, the discipline of software engineering is in crisis, and the author sees no reason quality will stop getting worse.
The default was already sloppy and poorly considered, and now everyone is frantically accelerating those same terrible practices to LLM speed.
His answer is a mainstream language designed for formal verification, and he argues the culture of software engineering has to change.
